exercise.name: Seated Knee Tuck
steps: Sit on a bench edge or the floor, leaning back on your hands.
Pull your knees in toward your chest as you lean slightly forward.
Push your legs back out straight without letting your feet touch down.
exercise.one_line_summary: Seated on the floor, leaning back ~45 deg on the hands behind the hips. Legs start long and hovering just off the floor; the knees pull in to the chest as the trunk comes ~7 deg more upright, then the legs push back out without the feet touching down. Rectus abdominis is the target; hip flexors do much of the leg work (not lit).

setup.target: Sit on the floor, hands on the floor behind the hips, arms nearly straight, trunk leaned back ~45 deg, back straight.
setup.why: Library step 1; Spotebi: hands on the mat, trunk leaned back, back straight.

setup.target: Legs long and together, lifted so the heels hover a few cm to ~20 cm off the floor.
setup.tolerance: leg line 5-20 deg above the floor; heels never touch
setup.why: Library step 3 and S1: extend without touching the mat.

movement.path: Knees draw straight in toward the chest, feet stay off the floor.
Thighs come up as the knees bend.

movement.end: 38 deg (leans slightly forward to meet the knees)
movement.path: Library step 2: lean slightly forward as the knees come in; back stays straight.

movement.start: planted ~0.5 m behind the hip joint, shoulder width
movement.path: Hands do not move; elbows straighten a little as the trunk comes up.
movement.tolerance: hands within 0.03 m of the floor

muscles.emg: No EMG study of this exact move found. Close variant: V-sit (trunk and legs raised, seated) ~80% MVIC RA (Maeo, in S2).
muscles.role: Holds the pelvis and trunk while the legs move; curls the pelvis toward the ribs at the tuck.
muscles.surface: Vertical bands down the front of the belly.

muscles.emg: Rectus femoris is highest in leg-driven sit-up-type moves (S3); S1 lists hip flexors as secondary.
muscles.role: Lift and pull the thighs in; no mask exists, so not lit.
muscles.surface: Front of the hip and upper thigh.

muscles.role: Straighten the knees on the way out (S1 secondary).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Heels rest on the floor at the 'out' position.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Library and S1: the legs stay off the floor so the abs keep working.

mistakes.mistake: Rounded back / collapsing onto the hands
mistakes.why_it_matters: S1: keep the back straight and the upper body stable.

sources.what_it_gave: Hands on the mat, trunk leaned back, knees to chest, extend fully without touching the mat, back straight; primary abs, secondary hip flexors and quads.

sources.citation: Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM. 2020. Core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306. doi:10.3390/ijerph17124306
Escamilla RF, McTaggart MS, Fricklas EJ, et al. 2006. An electromyographic analysis of commercial and common abdominal exercises. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 36(2):45-57. doi:10.2519/jospt.2006.36.2.45
sources.what_it_gave: Rectus femoris highest in hip-driven exercises (bent-knee sit-up and leg-driven devices).

clip_check.target: knee 100-130 deg; heels > 0.01 m above floor
